hardware.job_scale: 1 to 82,944 nodes depending on resource group

login.auth: SSH v2, public-key only (Ed25519, ECDSA P-521, or RSA >=2048-bit); private keys are never uploaded — register the public key via the Fugaku website User Portal, or edit ~/.ssh/authorized_keys directly once you already have access
login.arm_login_node: A separate 'arm1' node (ssh arm1 from a normal login node) exists for Arm-native cross-building only — no pjsub/pjstat there
login.file_transfer: sftp/scp/WinSCP over the same login hostname; ftp and r-commands are prohibited

scheduler.acl_and_limits: pjacl --rg <rscgrp> (a resource group's node/elapse min-max-default for your account); pjstat --limit (your live concurrent-submission/node/core quotas)
scheduler.group_directive_note: The project group is never hardcoded: set spec.attributes.account, or configure defaults.group in ~/.hpc-agent/fugaku.json (or FUGAKU_GROUP). The shared 'fugaku' group every account belongs to is explicitly denied job submission — confirmed live via `pjacl --rg small` ("pjsub + deny g(fugaku)"). Run `id` to see your real project groups.
scheduler.no_stdout_override: pjsub has no flag to set a custom stdout/stderr path — output always lands at '<jobname>.<jobid>.out' / '.err' in the submission directory
scheduler.no_gpu: Fugaku's compute nodes have no GPUs; resources.gpus / gpu_cores_per_process must stay unset
scheduler.mpi_launch: mpiexec -n <N> inside the job script (only needed when more than one task is requested — Fugaku's own single-node sample script runs the executable directly with no mpiexec at all)

resource_groups.note: Node/elapse ranges below are the values documented in RIKEN's official user guide as of this port; they can differ per project and the full production list lives on the Fugaku website's 'Resource group configuration' page (not mirrored here — see PORTING.md §2 on why this repo doesn't auto-fetch it). Always confirm with `pjacl --rg <name>` for your own account before relying on a number here.
resource_groups.trial_project_note: The 'trial' group (the default Startup Project every new Fugaku account gets) can only submit to the spot-* resource groups (spot-small, spot-int, spot-large, spot-middle) — small/large/int are rejected under it. Check which project group a job will actually run under before offering small/large; run `id` to see whether the account has a real research-project group beyond 'trial'.

int.elapse_max: 06:00:00 (documented default; varies per project — this account's own pjacl reports up to 24:00:00)

spot-small.note: runs only on otherwise-idle nodes; excluded from fee-based projects

spot-large.note: capped at 4h guaranteed, up to 12h if uncontested

spot-int.note: capped at 4h guaranteed, up to 6h if uncontested

storage.concept: Layered storage: fast, ephemeral, LLIO-managed first-layer cache in front of persistent second-layer FEFS (Lustre). Data placed only in the first layer disappears at job end unless explicitly copied out.

home.note: too small to use as a job execution area — use the group data volume instead

group_share.note: cross-group sharing via ACL; shares the data+share quota

2ndfs.note: direct FEFS access, bypasses the LLIO cache

node_local_tmp.lifetime: created at job start, deleted at job end

shared_tmp.scope: shared across all nodes within the same job
shared_tmp.lifetime: created at job start, deleted at job end

storage.gfscache_declaration: A job touching any second-layer volume outside $HOME (or using Spack, also under /vol0004) must declare it via '#PJM -x PJM_LLIO_GFSCACHE=<volume>' — resolved from defaults.gfscache_volume in ~/.hpc-agent/fugaku.json (or FUGAKU_GFSCACHE), never hardcoded (per-project).
storage.backup: Fugaku does not back up user data — self-managed.

modules.fujitsu_compiler: Native/default toolchain, module lang/tcsds-* (Fujitsu Technical Computing Suite)
modules.gcc: Cross-compile GCC at /vol0004/apps/oss/gcc-arm-*/setup-env.sh on the login node, or native GCC on a compute node via Spack
modules.llvm: module load LLVM/llvmorg-* on either login node (cross) or compute node (native)
modules.spack: Available as a separate package manager, e.g. /vol0004/apps/oss/spack/share/spack/setup-env.sh
modules.cross_compilation_note: Compute nodes are A64FX/Arm; ordinary login nodes are Intel x86. Building a binary that runs in a batch job requires a cross compiler on the login node (Fujitsu, GCC-for-arm, or LLVM's cross_clangfx build) — plain gcc/clang on a login node targets the login node's own Intel CPU, not the compute nodes.
